sources.title: Madagascar and the Social Impacts of Drought
sources.organization: World Bank, Social Sustainability and Inclusion Global Practice
sources.temporal_coverage: World Bank monitoring of the 2018-2022 drought and recovery period in southern Madagascar.
sources.methodology: Blog summarizes four-monthly monitoring of a representative 480-person panel during 2020-2022.
sources.limitations: Blog summary; respondent perceptions, not recorded incidence or causal effects.

sources.title: Greening the Great South of Madagascar: How Communities Are Fighting Drought and Restoring Hope
sources.temporal_coverage: World Bank feature on Great South climate and livelihood conditions and MIONJO results, published 2 June 2025.
sources.methodology: World Bank project feature with local examples, project-reported restoration outputs and staff commentary.
sources.limitations: Feature story, not a full risk assessment or independent impact evaluation; project outputs and examples are agency-reported.

sources.title: Madagascar Advocacy Note for Humanitarian Response
sources.temporal_coverage: Humanitarian crisis overview and response planning in the October 2025 advocacy note, including shocks from late 2024 through 2025.
sources.methodology: Humanitarian Country Team advocacy note consolidating IPC, sector and partner situation information and response requirements.
sources.limitations: Advocacy and needs-planning document; projections to January 2026 have since elapsed and were not outcome-verified here.

sources.title: Speed Saves Lives: What Cyclone Gezani Reveals about the Value of Rapid and Flexible Financing for Children
sources.temporal_coverage: UNICEF report on Cyclone Gezani's 10 February 2026 impacts and response, published 19 June 2026.
sources.methodology: UNICEF retrospective account of reported government and partner impacts and response outputs.
sources.limitations: Agency-reported figures; not independently audited here.

claims.locator: Paragraphs on drought monitoring and reported violence against women
claims.paraphrase: At the 2021 drought peak, 47 percent of respondents reported worsening violence against women.
institutions: Global Studies Institute, California State University
claims.limitations: Perceived worsening, not a measured change in GBV incidence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The post says harder water and food tasks raised risk of violent repercussions.

claims.locator: Paragraph on communal violence, cattle raiding and livelihood stress
claims.paraphrase: The article reports cattle raiding and other opportunistic violence rose during the drought.
institutions: Global Studies Institute, California State University
claims.limitations: Respondents link hunger and poverty to these harms; no event-attribution estimate is given.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Survey respondents linked drought-period hunger and poverty to opportunistic cattle raids and other violence.

claims.locator: Paragraph on migration as last-resort coping and risks faced by women migrants
claims.paraphrase: Migration intensified after other household coping options failed; women migrants faced heightened GBV and trafficking risks.
institutions: Global Studies Institute, California State University
claims.limitations: No migration counts or destination breakdown.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The post links prolonged drought, intensified migration and women's protection risks.

claims.locator: Paragraphs describing Great South livelihood dependence, recurrent drought, flooding, winds and desertification
claims.paraphrase: The feature describes Great South households reliant on farming and fishing facing repeated drought and water scarcity, followed by damaging floods, stronger southern winds, drifting sand and desertification that undermine crops and livelihoods.
claims.limitations: This feature provides regional description and examples, not a systematic district-level risk assessment.

claims.locator: Paragraphs on MIONJO geographic coverage and restoration results
claims.paraphrase: By June 2025, the World Bank reported MIONJO served about 1.4 million people in 235 rural communes across Atsimo-Andrefana, Androy and Anosy; project partners had stabilized 1,500 hectares of dunes, reforested 330 hectares and established 24 nurseries.
claims.limitations: Counts are project-reported as of the feature's publication; no independent evaluation of durability or livelihood effects is presented.

claims.locator: PDF p.2, situation overview of overlapping shocks and 22 districts
claims.paraphrase: The October 2025 HCT note says 22 Grand Sud/Grand Sud-Est districts faced drought, cyclone and locust shocks since late 2024, damaging crops and livelihoods and leaving little recovery time.
claims.limitations: Multi-hazard impacts; climate's share of losses is not isolated.

claims.locator: PDF p.2, current/projected acute food insecurity
claims.paraphrase: The HCT projected Grand Sud IPC Phase 4 hunger would rise from 29,000 people to nearly 110,000 by January 2026.
claims.scenario: Humanitarian food-security projection to January 2026; no climate scenario specified.
claims.limitations: The projection period ended in January 2026; this extraction does not verify the realized figure.

claims.locator: PDF p.2, funding constraints and field-office closures
claims.paraphrase: The HCT said about US$96 million in anticipated 2025 funding was suspended or redirected; 15 NGO field offices, mostly in high-need districts, closed, shrinking coverage.
claims.limitations: The note attributes closures to funding cuts, not conflict.

claims.locator: Paragraphs 12-20, Cyclone Gezani exposure and damage on the east coast
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reports Cyclone Gezani affected over 478,000 people, including 203,000 children, and damaged more than 102,000 homes, 761 schools and 30 health facilities on Madagascar's east coast.
institutions: National Office for Risk and Disaster Management
claims.limitations: UNICEF notes Gezani damage was predominantly wind-driven, unlike the extensive flooding from Cyclone Fytia.

claims.locator: Paragraphs 28-30, school disruption and temporary displacement sites
claims.paraphrase: The article says nearly 60,000 children had learning disrupted and 20,854 people took refuge in temporary sites after Gezani, where protection concerns intensified.
claims.limitations: The report describes increased risks of violence and exploitation, not measured post-cyclone incident rates.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNICEF says crowding and limited services in temporary sites heightened children's risks of violence and exploitation.

claims.locator: Paragraphs 30-42, early warning, pre-arranged financing and response outputs
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF says advance forecasts, pre-positioned supplies and renewed 2026 parametric insurance supported rapid response; reported outputs included restored safe water for 15,879 people and child-friendly or psychosocial support for over 2,000 people.
claims.limitations: The UNICEF article attributes speed and outputs to preparedness and flexible finance but is not an independent evaluation.

access_audit.locator: Full World Bank blog inspected, especially paragraphs on survey design, violence against women, cattle raiding and migration.
access_audit.notes: The author is a World Bank social development specialist; respondent perceptions are not described as administrative incident data.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.locator: Full World Bank feature inspected, particularly regional climate/livelihood description and MIONJO scope and outputs.
access_audit.notes: Project outputs and local examples are presented by the World Bank as reported results, not independent impact estimates.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.locator: Full 17-page HCT Advocacy Note inspected, including PDF p.2 on overlapping shocks, food-security projections, funding reductions and field closures.
access_audit.notes: Claims retain the source's reporting dates; January 2026 projections are not described as current outcomes.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

access_audit.locator: Full UNICEF story inspected, especially paragraphs 18-42 on Gezani impacts, protection risks, preparedness and response outputs.
access_audit.notes: The story attributes reported protection risks, operational actions and service outputs; they are not independently audited here.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrase only.

search_audit.query: Madagascar named districts and communities affected by drought, cyclones, flooding, food insecurity and service disruption, official UN and World Bank reports
search_audit.outcome: UN HCT, UNICEF and World Bank materials identify multi-hazard exposure in the Grand Sud/Grand Sud-Est and east coast, with named local examples and project areas; the HCT note reports 22 affected districts without listing all district names.

search_audit.query: Madagascar southern drought direct source-stated links to gender-based violence, cattle raiding, migration and child protection
search_audit.outcome: The World Bank's survey-summary blog reports perceived violence against women and respondent-linked opportunistic cattle raiding and migration risks during the 2018-2022 drought; UNICEF separately describes heightened child-protection risks after 2026 cyclone displacement.

search_audit.query: Madagascar official sources on banditry, insecurity or violence affecting humanitarian access during drought and climate response
search_audit.outcome: The OCHA Global Humanitarian Overview PDF could not be opened, so indexed search text was treated only as a lead and excluded from evidence. Reviewed accessible sources do not show FCV blocking a named climate-adaptation project.

search_audit.query: Madagascar local climate adaptation, Great South land restoration, cyclone preparedness and response capacity official results
search_audit.outcome: World Bank reports MIONJO landscape-restoration outputs in three southern regions; UNICEF reports preparedness, early warning, pre-positioned supplies, pre-arranged financing and post-Gezani service restoration. HCT reports funding reductions and an expired 2025-26 response plan/projection.

gaps: OCHA's Global Humanitarian Overview 2022 PDF returned 403; indexed text was excluded, leaving an evidence gap on insecurity and humanitarian access during drought.
The World Bank drought-monitoring article summarizes respondent perceptions and reported social trends, not official violence rates or causal estimates; its drought period was 2018-2022.
The HCT note's January 2026 food-insecurity forecast is historical by the October 2026 access date; no subsequent measured outcome was reviewed.
The HCT note does not enumerate all 22 affected districts, and the reviewed sources do not demonstrate FCV preventing implementation of a specific climate-adaptation intervention.
MIONJO feature and UNICEF cyclone story are agency-reported results; no independent project impact evaluation was reviewed for the reported outputs.
